def: A melatonin receptor agonist (MT1 and MT2) used for non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder in blind people.
A descending pathway from the superior colliculus that crosses in the midbrain and coordinates reflex head and neck movements toward visual and auditory stimuli.
A GLP-2 analog that promotes intestinal growth and absorption, used to treat short bowel syndrome.
A polymer in gram-positive bacterial cell walls that helps anchor the wall and, along with lipoteichoic acid, stimulates inflammatory responses.
Describes small dilated blood vessels visible on the skin or mucosa, as in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia or scleroderma.
A tellurium-containing agar supplement that selectively grows Corynebacterium diphtheriae, whose colonies turn black.
An inhibitor of tryptophan hydroxylase that lowers serotonin production, used for carcinoid syndrome diarrhea.
A bacteriophage enzyme that cuts concatemeric viral DNA and packages it into the phage head.
A growth hormone-releasing hormone analog used to reduce excess abdominal fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
A highly toxic dioxin contaminant (TCDD) in Agent Orange that activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor, causing chloracne and cancer risk.
Relating to fiber pathways that carry information from the thalamus to the cerebral cortex.
Small veins draining the myocardium directly into the heart chambers, mostly the right atrium and ventricle, contributing to physiologic shunt.
The enzyme succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA transferase that lets extrahepatic tissues use ketone bodies; liver lacks it, so it cannot burn ketones.
A branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus supplying the latissimus dorsi; it runs with the thoracodorsal artery.
A superficial vein of the lateral trunk that links the femoral and axillary systems, enlarging as a collateral in vena cava obstruction.
Relating to the thoracic and lumbar spine, as in the thoracolumbar sympathetic outflow from T1 to L2.
Preventive measures, such as heparin or compression stockings, used to prevent venous thrombosis in at-risk patients.
A developing T cell in the thymus that undergoes positive and negative selection before leaving as a mature T cell.
Relating to the thyroid cartilage and hyoid bone, as in the thyrohyoid membrane pierced by the internal laryngeal nerve.
Atrophic renal tubules filled with pink colloid-like casts that resemble thyroid follicles, seen in chronic pyelonephritis.
Relating to the thyropharyngeus, the upper part of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor that attaches to the thyroid cartilage.
A monoclonal antibody against the p19 subunit of interleukin-23, used for plaque psoriasis.
A topical microtubule and Src kinase inhibitor used to treat actinic keratosis on the face or scalp.
Measurement of pressure inside the eye, used to screen for glaucoma.
The spatial arrangement of sound frequencies along the cochlea and auditory pathway, with high frequencies at the base and low at the apex.
Formation of a mesh of ridges in a wall, such as thickened bladder wall muscle bundles from chronic outlet obstruction.
Transfer of an amino group from an amino acid to an alpha-keto acid, catalyzed by aminotransferases (ALT, AST) using vitamin B6.
Performed through a catheter, as in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
To introduce foreign DNA or RNA into cultured eukaryotic cells in the laboratory.
The cross-linking of peptidoglycan strands in bacterial cell walls by penicillin-binding proteins, which beta-lactam antibiotics inhibit.
Transfer of a phosphate group from one molecule to another, as when one kinase subunit phosphorylates its partner.
A form of amphibole asbestos linked to mesothelioma and asbestosis.
The blood-sucking kissing bug that transmits Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas disease) through feces rubbed into the bite.
A hairball in the stomach from swallowed hair, seen in Rapunzel syndrome, usually in young women with trichotillomania.
A sexually transmitted infection caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, producing frothy yellow-green discharge and strawberry cervix; treated with metronidazole.
The pathway carrying facial pain, temperature and touch from the trigeminal nuclei to the contralateral thalamus.
The three-layered embryonic disc of ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm formed during gastrulation in the third week.
A dye that stains viable tissue with intact dehydrogenases brick red, leaving dead tissue pale; used to identify myocardial infarcts on autopsy.
Labeled with tritium, a radioactive hydrogen isotope, as in tritiated thymidine used to track DNA synthesis.
A pulley-like structure, such as the trochlea of the orbit through which the superior oblique tendon passes, or the humeral trochlea that articulates with the ulna.
Yellow-orange nodules on extensor surfaces such as elbows and knees, seen in familial dysbetalipoproteinemia and other high-cholesterol states.
A pus-filled collection involving the fallopian tube and ovary, a complication of pelvic inflammatory disease.
Describes membrane structures that combine tubes and vesicles, as in the cristae of mitochondria in steroid-producing cells.
Drum-like, hollow percussion sound heard over air-filled bowel or a pneumothorax.
Tagged with ubiquitin, a small protein that marks other proteins for degradation by the proteasome.
A substance, such as 2,4-dinitrophenol or thermogenin, that dissipates the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane so the energy escapes as heat instead of making ATP.
A person who excretes too little uric acid in urine, the main mechanism for hyperuricemia and gout.
Having incompletely developed male characteristics, as in XY individuals with androgen deficiency or insensitivity.
